SMTO-CFG-0095 — SMTO couldn't continue the task after your Skill answer

GUID: fa9aded8-928a-5148-88fc-ec98a04acff7
Slug: capability-activation-continuation-failed
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: capability_activation

What happened

  • After you answered the Skill permission question, SMTO couldn't save the next step that carries the task on. The task may not have continued yet.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the page and look under the task for new activity. If it is running or has finished, it already continued and you don't need to do anything. Answering again after it already continued could start the same work twice.
  2. If the permission question is still showing and nothing new is running, answer it once more. An open question means the next step was never saved, so answering again is safe.
  3. If it fails again, ask the person who manages SMTO to check that the computer running SMTO has free disk space and that SMTO can write to its data folder. SMTO needs to save the next step before the task can carry on.

What success looks like

  • The task shows new activity after your answer, and only one copy of it is running.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details in this panel and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't send the same request again as a new message until they confirm the task didn't continue; that could repeat its actions.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The continuation run that should resume the task after a capability grant decision could not be saved (no current code path raises this kind directly; grant-driven continuation is created inside the grant transaction).

What this means

  • This retained continuation-failure kind has no direct current producer; grant-driven continuation is created inside the owning grant transaction. The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.

Why this can happen

  • This retained continuation-failure kind has no direct current producer; grant-driven continuation is created inside the owning grant transaction.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the original grant and any existing child continuation before requesting another.

How to fix it

  • Check the parent run's capability_grants entry and capability_grant_child binding for an existing continuation before creating another. Resolve the storage or transaction failure shown in the Server log, then resubmit the decision only if the grant is still prompted, so at most one continuation owns execution.
  • Check the original grant and continuation state, resolve the actual failure and reuse the supported existing interaction without duplicating a child run.

Retry and execution caution

  • The reported capability or interaction condition changes.

How to verify the fix

  • The original grant/child binding is reconciled and at most one accepted continuation owns execution.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass frozen authority, operation permissions or credential requirements.

Technical notes

  • The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
